questions.prompt: In BayPay’s payment-service, which type is actually a Jakarta servlet?

choices.text: PaymentController
DispatcherServlet
PaymentApplicationService
PaymentRepository

questions.explanation: Spring MVC’s DispatcherServlet is an HttpServlet. PaymentController is a handler the dispatcher invokes. Services and repositories are not servlets.

questions.prompt: Which pairing is the best Spring → Jakarta mapping for BayPay’s write path?

choices.text: @RestController ↔ JTA; @Transactional ↔ JAX-RS
JpaRepository ↔ EntityManager; @Transactional ↔ JTA demarcation
application.yml ↔ EntityManager; JpaRepository ↔ JNDI
Spring IoC ↔ JMS; ApplicationEventPublisher ↔ CDI only

questions.explanation: Spring Data repositories call an EntityManager. @Transactional is Spring’s facade over JTA-like begin/commit/rollback. YAML maps to JNDI as a binding mechanism, not to JPA.

questions.prompt: Hikari on pay-prod-east-2 shows active 50 / max 50 and 41 waiters. Database CPU is 19%. What does this establish?

choices.text: PostgreSQL is down.
The JVM heap is exhausted.
This instance’s pool is exhausted; the cause is not yet proven.
You must raise maximum-pool-size to 200 immediately.

questions.explanation: 50/50 plus waiters is exhaustion — a symptom. Low DB CPU argues against a dead database. Raising max is not a diagnosis.

questions.prompt: A Hikari leak-detection line appears in logs. How should an on-call engineer treat it?

choices.text: As proof the root cause is a connection leak.
As a candidate: confirm checkout age, stacks, and whether connections return.
As a reason to disable leak detection in production.
As evidence the JNDI name is wrong.

questions.explanation: Leak detection flags checkouts that exceed a threshold. Long legitimate statements can trip it. Stacks and whether in-use stays high after traffic drops turn a candidate into a conclusion.

questions.prompt: POST /api/v1/payments returns 201 with status COMPLETED, but ledger_transactions has no row for that payment id. What class of failure is this until proven otherwise?

choices.text: Load-balancer TLS mismatch
Connection pool exhaustion
A transaction-boundary split between status and ledger
Missing HttpSession replication

questions.explanation: HTTP success plus COMPLETED without a ledger row means two units of work disagreed. Pool exhaustion would typically fail the HTTP call. Sessions are not part of the payment API.

questions.prompt: Why should a new BayPay service not look up jdbc/baypay from a traditional WAS cell JNDI tree as its default design?

choices.text: JNDI cannot represent a DataSource.
Spring Boot cannot use a DataSource.
Traditional WAS ND is a source estate to modernize from, not a greenfield runtime.
JNDI names are illegal in Kubernetes.

questions.explanation: JNDI is valid historical binding and still appears on the existing cell (Module 5). Greenfield BayPay services should use Boot or Liberty with externalized config, not grow the ND cell.

questions.prompt: Why does BayPay’s payment API avoid HttpServletRequest.getSession(true)?

choices.text: Jakarta EE forbids sessions.
The conversation is the Idempotency-Key plus rows in the database; a session would force affinity or replication.
Spring MVC cannot read cookies.
Sessions are only available on WebSphere ND.

questions.explanation: Stateless APIs scale without sticky sessions. Money state belongs in the database. Sessions still exist on some legacy portal ears; they are not a payment-API feature.

questions.prompt: A deploy adds REQUIRES_NEW on PaymentPostingService.postAuthorized while create() stays @Transactional. What is the risk?

choices.text: The HTTP thread can no longer run filters.
Payment COMPLETED can commit while the ledger unit rolls back independently.
JNDI lookups start failing.
Hikari automatically sets max pool size to 1.

questions.explanation: REQUIRES_NEW suspends the caller’s transaction and starts another. The two commits are independent. That is the INCIDENT-403 mechanism.
